Select K by silhouette width or the gap statistic

Source: R/select_K.R
select_K.Rd

Select K by silhouette width or the gap statistic

Usage

select_K(
  Z,
  K_range = 2:8,
  method = c("silhouette", "gap"),
  base = c("pam", "rankkmed"),
  B_gap = 20L,
  distance = c("rho", "dF")
)

Arguments

Z

Complex pre-shape matrix (k-1) x n, or an n x n distance matrix (silhouette only: the gap statistic needs the pre-shapes to draw its null reference).

K_range

Integer vector of candidate values of K.

method

One of "silhouette" (default) or "gap".

base

Base clusterer to use for each candidate K. One of "pam" (default) or "rankkmed".

B_gap

Number of null reference samples for the gap statistic.

distance

One of "rho" (default), "dF".

Value

A list with:

K_hat

Selected K.

scores

Named numeric vector of scores (silhouette width or gap statistic) at each candidate K.

se

For "gap", the simulation standard errors \(s_K\); NULL otherwise.

method

Selection method used.

Details

The gap statistic compares \(\log W_K\) with its mean under B_gap samples of the same size drawn uniformly on the shape space (uniform pre-shapes, i.e. a Complex Bingham with zero concentration). The selected K is the smallest one with \(\mathrm{Gap}(K) \ge \mathrm{Gap}(K') - s_{K'}\), where \(K'\) is the next candidate (Tibshirani, Walther and Hastie, 2001).

References

Rousseeuw, P. J. (1987). Silhouettes: a graphical aid to the interpretation and validation of cluster analysis. Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics, 20, 53–65. doi:10.1016/0377-0427(87)90125-7

Tibshirani, R., Walther, G. and Hastie, T. (2001). Estimating the number of clusters in a data set via the gap statistic. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society B, 63(2), 411–423. doi:10.1111/1467-9868.00293

Examples

set.seed(1)
# Three clusters
mu_list <- list(
  matrix(c(0,0, 10,0, 10,10, 0,10), 4, 2, byrow = TRUE),
  matrix(c(0,0, 20,0, 20,10, 0,10), 4, 2, byrow = TRUE),
  matrix(c(0,0, 15,0, 10,10, 0,10), 4, 2, byrow = TRUE)
)
out <- sim_landmark_gaussian(mu_list, c(15, 15, 15), sigma = 0.5)
Z <- landmarks_to_preshape(out$X)
res <- select_K(Z, K_range = 2:5, method = "silhouette")
res$K_hat
#> [1] 3
